newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria ponders leasing steel plants to investors.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria ponders leasing steel plants to investors.

text.p: Nigeria is considering new proposals to lease its troubled steel plants to private investors, steel minister Bashir Dalhatu said on Wednesday.
"A leasing option is being considered for the three inland steel rolling mills and Delta Steel Company," he told reporters in Lagos, adding that a final decision would soon be announced.
The option of leasing the steel plants to private investors was first considered in 1995 but apparently no investors were ready to take up the offer because of the poor state of the plants.
The plants commenced operation 15 years ago but their output has remained at less than 25 percent of installed capacity.

While Delta Steel, located in the midwestern oil town of Warri has a capacity to produce one million tonnes of liquid steel, the rolling mill located in the south-west and two others in the north have a combined capacity of 280,000 metric tonnes of steel products a year.
The fifth and biggest steel plant at Ajaokuta in central Nigeria, remains uncompleted after 18 years construction.
"The major handicap of Ajaokuta Steel is the high debt profile, non-completion of external infrastructure and loss of manpower," the minister said.
He said the government had set aside 6.6 billion naira for work on the project this year.
